question: What is the reason behind the Indian peninsular region not showing drastic change during winters and having a moderate temperature?

options.text: moderating Influence of dense human population

solution:
The correct answer is __**moderating Influence of the sea**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian peninsular region is surrounded by the **Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal, and the Indian Ocean** on three sides, which significantly influence its climate.
 
• The presence of these large water bodies **moderates the temperature** and prevents extreme fluctuations.
 
• During winters, the sea retains heat and warms the coastal areas, resulting in a **moderate climate**.
 
• This phenomenon is known as the **moderating influence of the sea**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **peninsular region** of India includes states such as Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, and Maharashtra.
 
• These areas experience a **tropical maritime climate** due to the influence of the surrounding seas.
 
• In addition to moderating temperatures, the sea also brings in moisture-laden winds, contributing to the **monsoon season**.
 
• This climatic feature is crucial for the **agriculture and overall ecology** of the region.
